docs.title: Stats Collector manual
docs.text:
Stats Collector collects reach, engagement and audience numbers from your website, social media and streams, and combines them in one dashboard and in reports. This manual explains how to install it, how to set everything up, and how to connect each platform.

The same manual opens inside the application through the Help button at the bottom of the left menu. The version there always matches the installed version.

This manual grows with every release. Pages for connectors that are not built yet describe the preparation you can already do, so the accounts are ready when the connector arrives.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: Troubleshooting lists the log files, the command line tools and the most common problems.

docs.title: Backup and restore
docs.text: Administration → Backup & restore makes full and incremental backups of the database and the files (uploaded logos and the configuration file) and copies them to one or more remote locations.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The database is backed up with pgBackRest. A full backup contains everything; an incremental backup only what changed since the previous backup. PostgreSQL archives its transaction log continuously, so backups are consistent while the app keeps running.
  • Files are packed with tar in incremental mode.
  • After each backup the complete local backup folder (/var/lib/stats-collector/backup) is synchronised with rclone to every enabled remote location.
  • With an encryption passphrase the copies on the remote location are encrypted (rclone crypt: XSalsa20-Poly1305). Without the passphrase nobody can read them, including you, so store it in your password manager.

docs.title: Remote locations
docs.text:
Click Add location and choose a protocol:

Protocol When to use Notes SCP / SFTP (SSH) NAS, Linux server, hosting with SSH Password or private key (OpenSSH or PEM format). On the first Test the server's host key is stored and checked from then on. FTPS NAS or hosting with FTP over TLS Explicit (port 21, AUTH TLS) is most common; implicit uses port 990. FTP Only on a trusted network The password is sent unencrypted.

Folder is the path on the remote server; it is created automatically. Click Test to check the connection: the log shows each step and the backups already stored there.

docs.title: Schedule and retention
docs.text:
• Make backups automatically: on or off.
  • Full backup every day, week (choose the day) or month, at the chosen time (time zone from General settings).
  • Incremental backup every N hours in between.
  • Keep full backups: how many full backups (with their incrementals) are kept. Older ones are removed locally and on the remote locations.

Full backup now and Incremental backup now start one immediately. The log appears on the page.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
1. Under Restore choose a location and click Show backups. The list comes from the remote location itself, so this also works on a brand new server.
  2. Click Restore next to the moment you want to go back to. Choosing an incremental backup restores the full backup plus all incrementals up to that point.
  3. Type RESTORE and confirm. The application stops, the database and files are replaced, and the application starts again. Sign in again afterwards.

docs.title: Disaster recovery on a new server
docs.text:
1. Install Stats Collector on the new server with the installer.
  2. Create a temporary administrator through the setup link.
  3. Under Backup & restore set the same encryption passphrase and add the remote location.
  4. Show the backups and restore the newest one. The restored configuration contains the original secret key, so stored passwords keep working.

docs.title: Before every update
docs.text: Updates from the interface make an extra database dump in /var/lib/stats-collector/backup/pre-update/ first and use it to roll back automatically if the update fails.

docs.title: Branding
docs.text:
Administration → Branding sets the look of the application, reports, emails and the live wall.

  • Name and logo: application name, a logo for light backgrounds, a logo for dark backgrounds (used in the dark menu) and the browser icon. SVG, PNG, WebP or ICO up to 2 MB. SVG files that contain scripts are refused.
  • Colours: accent, background, cards, menu, text, lines and the status colours, separately for light and dark mode. The preview updates while you change them. Text on the accent colour switches between black and white automatically for readability.
  • Colours per channel: the colour of each platform in charts (website, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Owncast, Icecast).
  • Typography and shape: heading and body font, corner radius of cards and buttons.

Click Save to apply the brand for everyone. Back to default restores the built-in brand from branding/default/theme.json.

docs.title: Export, import and the repository
docs.text: Export brand downloads a theme.json. Commit it to the project repository as branding/<name>/theme.json together with the logo files, so every brand is versioned. Import brand loads such a file; click Save afterwards.

docs.title: Light and dark mode
docs.text: Each user chooses System, Light or Dark under My profile → Appearance. System follows the computer's setting.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
Analytics → Content lists the articles, broadcasts and streams with the most views or listening and watching minutes in the chosen period (24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, or 12 months). Everyone can open it.

  • Search titles, Source, Category and Editor narrow the list. The editor filter is there only for roles that may see editors (see below).
  • Sort orders by views, visitors, reading time, read, shares, comments, listening/watching minutes, or shows the newest items first.

  • Columns: Views, Visitors, Avg. reading time (reading time divided by views), Read, Shares and Listen/watch min. for broadcasts and mount points. See WordPress for what each number means.

  • Facebook and Instagram posts and YouTube videos are in the same list. For a post, Visitors / reach shows its reach. See Meta and YouTube for how their numbers are collected.

Click an item for its details: the numbers for the period, a chart per day (per hour for 24 hours), and for an article where readers came from and the devices they used. A Facebook post also shows its reactions per type (like, love, wow…); an Instagram post its saves.

docs.title: Editors
docs.text:
Analytics → Editors shows the numbers per editor: how many of their articles were published in the period, and the views, visitors, reading time, reads, shares and comments of all their articles in that period. An article with two authors counts for both.

The Social views column adds up the views of the Facebook and Instagram posts and YouTube videos that link to the editor's articles (see Posts linked to articles). Click an editor for a chart, their best-read articles and their social numbers per platform, with the linked posts.

docs.title: Posts linked to articles
docs.text:
A Facebook post, Instagram post or YouTube video is linked to an article automatically when it points to the article's address:

  • Facebook: the link attached to the post, or a link in its text.
  • Instagram: a link in the caption (Instagram links usually sit in the bio, so link these by hand when needed).
  • YouTube: a link in the video description.

Addresses are compared without https://, www. or a trailing /, and without tracking parameters such as utm_source or fbclid; Facebook's redirect links are followed to the real address. The short link ?p=123 of a WordPress post works too. Links are checked every 15 minutes, after new posts have been collected.

Open an article to see the posts and videos that link to it under Shared on social media, with their views, reach, likes and shares, and the total as Social views. A post shows its Linked article. Click a title to open that item.

Admins, editors-in-chief and editors can change links:

  • Add link searches articles (from a post) or posts and videos (from an article) by title or address; click a result to link it. The link is marked by hand.
  • The unlink button removes a link. A removed automatic link stays removed, also when the post is collected again; adding it by hand brings it back.

An editor's social numbers include every post linked to one of their articles. A post linked to an article with two authors counts for both.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
Editor names and per-editor numbers are removed by the server before anything reaches the browser, so they cannot be found in the page either.

Role Content Editors Admin, Editor-in-chief All items, with editor names and the editor filter Everyone Editor All items, without editor names Only their own numbers Staff All items, without editor names Not available

An editor sees their own numbers when their Stats Collector account has the same email address as their WordPress user. Under Editors, Not linked to a user means no account with that email address exists yet.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The dashboard is the first screen after signing in. Everyone can open it, whatever their role.

docs.title: Website and video
docs.text: When a WordPress site, YouTube channel, Facebook Page or Instagram account is connected, the dashboard starts with the card Website and video: the views of all channels together with their total reach, a tile per website (page views and visitors), per YouTube channel (views, minutes watched, subscribers and how many were gained in the period) and per Facebook Page or Instagram account (views, reach, followers and how many were gained), and a chart with the views per hour (24 hours) or per day, stacked per channel. YouTube numbers arrive one to two days late, so the last days of the chart fill in later. YouTube, Facebook and Instagram only report whole days: in the 24 hours view their tiles say daily numbers only and they are left out of the chart. Top content opens the Content page.

docs.title: Live now
docs.text:
• Live now: everyone listening and watching at this moment, over all sources. The red dot pulses while at least one source is on air.
  • Peak today: the highest audience of each source today, added up.
  • Listening and viewing minutes and Highest peak: totals for the period you picked at the top right (24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days).

Below that is a tile per source with the audience right now and today's peak. For an Icecast server with several mount points each mount is listed; for Owncast you see the title of the running broadcast. A red line in a tile means the last poll failed; the reason is shown, and Administration → Sources has the details.

The tiles refresh every 15 seconds.

docs.title: Live audience chart
docs.text:
• Average, Peak, Minutes: what the chart shows. Average is the number of people listening or watching at the same time, Minutes the total time listened and watched.
  • Stacked adds the sources up into one total, Overlay draws them over each other, Separate gives each source its own small chart.
  • Click a name in the legend below the chart to hide or show that source.

For 24 hours every point is 5 minutes, for 7 days one hour, for 30 and 90 days one day. Days follow the time zone under General settings.

docs.title: Per source and top broadcasts
docs.text: Per source lists minutes, average and peak per source in the period. Top broadcasts and streams shows the Owncast broadcasts and Icecast mounts with the most minutes.

docs.title: How the numbers are counted
docs.text:
Every source is polled every 30 seconds (adjustable per source). Each poll stores the number of listeners or viewers at that moment. Every 5 minutes these samples are summed into hourly, daily and monthly totals:

  • minutes = listeners × time between two polls;
  • average = minutes divided by the length of the hour or day (time off air counts as zero);
  • peak = the highest number seen in a single poll.

If the collector itself was down, that gap is not filled in. Raw samples are kept for one year; hourly and daily totals are kept forever.

docs.title: My dashboards
docs.text: Analytics → My dashboards lets you build your own views of the numbers: totals, charts per platform or per source, top content, the editors ranking and goals, side by side. Everyone can make dashboards for themselves; admins and editors-in-chief can also share a dashboard with everyone.

docs.title: Using a dashboard
docs.text:
• The tabs at the top are your dashboards and the shared ones (marked with the share icon). The app remembers which one you opened last.
  • The period at the top right (24 hours, 7, 30 or 90 days, 12 months) applies to every widget.
  • A total shows the number for the period and how much it went up or down against the period before (for 30 days: the 30 days before that).
  • A chart can be switched between Stacked (the lines add up to one total), Overlay (lines over each other) and Separate (a small chart per platform or source). Anyone can switch; only someone who may edit the dashboard saves it as the default.
  • Click a name in the legend below a chart to hide or show it.
  • In Top content, click a title for its details.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
Every platform's numbers are added up in five shared measures, so channels can be stacked into one total:

Measure Counts Reach Website visitors plus Facebook and Instagram reach Views Page views, YouTube views and Facebook and Instagram post views Interactions Likes, reactions, comments, shares and saves (website: shares and comments) Watch and listen minutes YouTube watch minutes plus Owncast and Icecast minutes Followers YouTube subscribers plus Facebook and Instagram followers, per day

Reach is counted per day, so someone who comes back on two days counts twice. YouTube, Facebook and Instagram only report whole days: with 24 hours they are left out of a chart (the widget says so), and Followers always shows days.

docs.title: Building a dashboard
docs.text:
Click New dashboard, or Edit on a dashboard you may change. With no dashboards yet, Create an example dashboard gives you a ready-made start (reach, views and interactions, reach per platform, followers, interactions, top content and editors) that you can change.

While editing:

  • Type the dashboard's name at the top. Shared with everyone (admins and editors-in-chief) makes it visible to all users; only admins, editors-in-chief and its maker can change it.
  • Add widget opens the widget form. Each widget has arrows to move it up or down, a pencil to change it and a bin to remove it.
  • Save stores the dashboard, Cancel drops the changes, Delete removes the whole dashboard.

The widget form:

  • Widget: Total (KPI), Chart, Top content, Editors ranking or Goals.
  • Width: a third, half or the full width. On a phone every widget takes the full width.
  • Title: leave it empty to use the measure's name.
  • Measure, Platforms and Sources (total and chart): what to count, and from where. Nothing selected means all.
  • Lines per (chart): one line per platform, per source, or one total. View and Chart (area, line or bars) set how it is drawn.
  • Sort by, Items and Number of rows (top content): for example the 10 most-read articles or the social posts with the most reach.

The Editors ranking shows editor numbers only to roles that may see them (see Content and editors).

docs.title: Email (SMTP)
docs.text: Stats Collector sends notifications and (from phase 4) reports through your own SMTP server. Open Administration → Email.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Field Explanation Send email Master switch SMTP server, port e.g. smtp.office365.com and 587 Encryption STARTTLS (port 587, recommended), SSL/TLS (SMTPS, port 465) or none (only on a trusted local network). TLS 1.2 is the minimum. Verify the server certificate Leave on. Only switch off for an internal server with a self-signed certificate. Authentication Username and password, OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2) or none From address, name, reply-to What recipients see

The buttons Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and SMTPS (465) fill in the server, port and encryption.

Passwords and secrets are stored encrypted. The screen only shows that a value is stored; leave the field empty to keep it.

docs.title: Test
docs.text: Enter an address under Test and click Send test email. The settings are saved first. If sending fails, the exact error from the mail server is shown, for example 535 Authentication unsuccessful.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 with OAuth 2.0
docs.text:
Microsoft is switching off basic authentication for SMTP. Use OAuth 2.0 instead:

  1. In the Entra admin center go to App registrations → New registration, name it Stats Collector mail.
  2. API permissions → Add a permission → APIs my organization uses → Office 365 Exchange Online → Application permissions → SMTP.SendAsApp. Click Grant admin consent.
  3. Certificates & secrets → New client secret. Copy the value.
  4. In Exchange Online PowerShell register the app and give it rights on the sending mailbox: 
    New-ServicePrincipal -AppId <client-id> -ObjectId <enterprise-app-object-id>
Add-MailboxPermission -Identity stats@example.org -User <enterprise-app-object-id> -AccessRights FullAccess
  5. In Stats Collector choose OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2):
  6. Username: the mailbox, e.g. stats@example.org
  7. Token URL: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/v2.0/token
  8. Scope: https://outlook.office365.com/.default
  9. Client ID and client secret from steps 1 and 3
  10. Send a test email.

Sending through the Microsoft Graph API (instead of SMTP) arrives with the reports in phase 4.

docs.title: Followers
docs.text:
Analytics → Followers shows how the number of YouTube subscribers and Facebook and Instagram followers grows, per channel and for all channels together. Everyone can open it.

  • Pick 30 days, 90 days or 12 months at the top right.
  • The tiles show the count now, how much it changed in the period and how many new followers came in (people who left are not subtracted in that last number).
  • Stacked shows the channels on top of each other, so the top line is the total; Separate shows each channel on its own scale.

The count per day is the count at the end of that day. YouTube and Facebook give the daily gains and losses for their whole history, so their lines go back as far as the history import. Instagram gives new followers for the last 30 days only; its line becomes exact from the day you connected it. See YouTube and Meta.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
Analytics → Goals lists the goals with their progress. Everyone can see them; the editor-in-chief and administrators can add and change them.

A goal measures one of these, over all channels or the channels you pick:

Measure The goal is reached when Followers the number of followers and subscribers reaches the target Views page, video and post views since the start date add up to the target Reach website visitors and social reach per day since the start date add up to the target Interactions likes, reactions, comments, shares and saves since the start date add up to the target Listening and watching minutes live minutes and YouTube watch time since the start date add up to the target

Each goal card shows the value now, the target, a progress bar and a status:

  • On track: at the pace of the last two weeks the target is reached by the end date;
  • Behind: at that pace it is not;
  • Reached and Not reached (the end date has passed).

Click a goal for the details: the current pace and the pace needed per day, the forecast for the end date, and a chart with the value, the target as a dashed line and the trend as a dotted line.

docs.title: Adding and changing a goal
docs.text:
1. New goal: a name, what to measure, the target, a start date and (optionally) an end date. Select channels, or none for all channels.
  2. Tick Email when the goal is reached or falls behind to get a message. Without addresses it goes to whoever made the goal. The emails go out via the mail server under Administration → Email; a goal that falls behind is reported at most once a week.
  3. You can change the target or end date at any time. Every change is kept in the target history with the date, who made it and the reason. The chart shows the target that applied at each moment, so reports stay honest about what the target was then.
  4. Archive a goal that is finished to move it out of the list; it stays under Archived.

The dashboard shows the active goals with their progress bars under Goals.

docs.title: Installation on Debian 13
docs.text: Stats Collector runs on a dedicated Debian 13 (Trixie) server or virtual machine. The installer sets up everything: database, background services, backups and the application itself.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Minimum Recommended CPU 2 cores 4 cores Memory 4 GB 8 GB Disk 20 GB 50 GB or more (backups and one year of raw data) Operating system Debian 13, freshly installed Network Outgoing HTTPS to GitHub, Debian and the platform APIs

The server needs a host name that users can reach through your reverse proxy, for example stats.example.org.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Log in as root (or use sudo -i) and run:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhisijmuiden/stats-collector/develop/install.sh -o install.sh
bash install.sh

The installer asks four questions. Press Enter to accept the default.

Question Meaning Update channel test follows new features first (default during development), production only stable releases. You can switch later in Info & updates. Public URL The address users type, e.g. https://stats.example.org. Reverse proxy IP addresses The IP of your Zoraxy (or other proxy). Only these addresses may tell the app the visitor's real IP. Web port / listen address Default 8080 on all interfaces. Use 127.0.0.1 when the proxy runs on the same server.

To install without questions:

bash install.sh --channel test --public-url https://stats.example.org --proxy-ips 192.0.2.10 -y

Add --client-ip-header CF-Connecting-IP when the public address goes through Cloudflare (see Reverse proxy).

Add --firewall to let nftables block port 8080 for everyone except the proxy.

docs.title: What the installer does
docs.text:
1. Checks that this is Debian 13, that you are root and that the network works.
  2. Installs Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, pgBackRest and rclone from the Debian repositories.
  3. Creates the system user statscollector, the folders /opt/stats-collector, /var/lib/stats-collector and /etc/stats-collector.
  4. Generates secrets in /etc/stats-collector/config.env, creates the database, and enables WAL archiving for incremental backups.
  5. Downloads the newest release of your channel from GitHub, checks its SHA-256 checksum and installs it with its own Python environment.
  6. Runs the database migrations and starts the services.
  7. Prints a one-time link to create the first administrator.

Running the installer again is safe. It keeps your configuration and repairs anything that is missing.

docs.title: First administrator
docs.text:
Open the link printed at the end, for example https://stats.example.org/setup?token=…, and create your account. The link works once and expires after 24 hours. Make a new one with:

stats-collector setup-link

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Service What it does stats-collector-web The web application and API on port 8080 stats-collector-worker Polls the sources (Icecast, Owncast) and adds up the numbers every 5 minutes stats-collector-ops.path / .service Runs updates, backups and restores that administrators start in the interface stats-collector-backup.timer Checks every hour whether a scheduled backup is due

Next step: Reverse proxy and HTTPS.

docs.title: Meta: Facebook and Instagram
docs.text:
Stats Collector reads the numbers of a Facebook Page and of an Instagram professional account (Business or Creator) through Meta's Graph API. One Meta app serves both. Each Page and each Instagram account is its own source, so you can add several.

What you need:

  • a Meta Business portfolio (Business Manager) that is verified (done for this project);
  • the Facebook Page you want to measure, with you as admin of it;
  • for Instagram: the Instagram professional account linked to that Page.

docs.title: What is collected
docs.text:
Per day for the Page or account Per post Facebook Views, reach, post engagements, reactions, comments, shares, clicks, video views, new followers, unfollows, followers Views, reach, reactions (also per type: like, love, wow…), comments, shares, clicks Instagram Views, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves, profile visits, new followers, followers Views, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves

Right after connecting, the history is imported: two years of Page numbers and all Facebook posts of those two years, and for Instagram the last 90 days of account numbers plus the posts of the last two years. After that the numbers are updated every hour.

Good to know:

  • Meta reports posts only as running totals. Stats Collector stores what a post gained per day; a post that is new to Stats Collector gets its whole total on the day it was published.
  • Instagram gives new followers only for the last 30 days and only for accounts with at least 100 followers, and does not report unfollows. The follower count per day is worked back from the count Stats Collector sees every hour, so it becomes exact from the day you connect.
  • Reach is the number of people who saw something. Summed over several days, a person who saw something on two days counts twice.
  • Meta works in whole days: in the dashboard's 24 hours view Facebook and Instagram show daily numbers only.

docs.title: 1. Create the app
docs.text:
1. Go to developers.facebook.com/apps → Create app.
  2. Use case: Other → app type Business.
  3. Name: Stats Collector, contact email, and select your verified Business portfolio.
  4. In App settings → Basic fill in the privacy policy URL, terms URL, app icon (1024×1024) and category Business and pages. Save. Here you also find the App ID and App secret (click Show).

docs.title: 2. Add Facebook Login for Business
docs.text:
1. Add product → Facebook Login for Business.
  2. Under Facebook Login for Business → Settings, paste the redirect address that Stats Collector shows in the source form (it ends in /api/connectors/meta/callback) into Valid OAuth Redirect URIs. Save.
  3. Optional: under Configurations you can create a configuration of type User access token with the permissions below. Paste its ID in the source form under Advanced → Configuration ID. Without it, Stats Collector asks for the permissions directly, which also works.

docs.title: 3. Permissions and App Review
docs.text:
Permission Why pages_show_list List the Pages the administrator manages pages_read_engagement Posts, reactions, comments, shares, followers read_insights Page and post insights (views, reach, clicks) business_management Pages owned by the Business portfolio instagram_basic Instagram account and posts instagram_manage_insights Instagram views, reach, saves, profile visits

While the app is in development mode it already works for people who have a role in the app (admin, developer or tester), which is enough to connect your own Page. For the app to keep working without that, request advanced access:

  1. App Review → Permissions and features: click Request advanced access for each permission above.
  2. For each, describe how it is used: "Stats Collector is an internal analytics dashboard for our newsroom. An administrator connects our own Page and Instagram account once; we read insights for our own content and show them to staff in dashboards and monthly reports. No data is shared with third parties."
  3. Upload a short screen recording of the steps below (connect with Facebook, choose the Page, the numbers under Content and on the dashboard).
  4. Complete Data handling questions and submit. Switch the app to Live after approval.

docs.title: 4. Add the source in Stats Collector
docs.text:
1. Administration → Sources → Add source, kind Facebook (Page) or Instagram (account).

  2. Fill in a name, the App ID and the App secret, and save.

  3. Click Connect with Facebook and sign in with an administrator of the Page. On Facebook's screen select the Page (and its Instagram account) and allow every permission.

  4. Back in Stats Collector:
    • with one Page (or one Instagram account) it is connected right away;
    • with several, the form asks Which Page? or Which Instagram account?. Pick one; add another source for each of the others. You can reuse the same App ID and secret.
  5. The history is imported in the background. The source list shows Importing history… until it is done.

The Page token Stats Collector receives does not expire, but it stops working when the administrator who connected it changes their Facebook password, loses their role on the Page or removes the app. The source then shows Access to Facebook has ended: click Connect with Facebook again.

Disconnect stops collecting and forgets the token; the numbers collected so far are kept.

docs.title: Advanced: Graph API version and metric names
docs.text:
Meta brings out a new Graph API version a few times a year and sometimes renames or removes metrics. Stats Collector:

  • uses a tested Graph API version, shown under Advanced; fill in another (for example v24.0) when Meta retires the one in use;
  • knows the old and new names of each metric and finds out by itself which one works, once per version;
  • marks metrics Meta no longer offers as not available under Advanced → Metric names.

When Meta announces a new name for a metric, fill it in next to that metric and save; Stats Collector tries it first.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text: Message What to do Facebook did not accept the code Check the App ID, App secret and that the redirect address is in Valid OAuth Redirect URIs exactly. This Facebook account manages no Page Connect again and select the Page on Facebook's screen (click Edit access if you connected before). None of the Pages … has an Instagram professional account Link the Instagram account to the Page (Instagram app → Settings → Account type, or Meta Business Suite), then connect again. Meta refused access A permission is missing or the app is still in development mode for someone without a role in the app. Meta asks to slow down Nothing: collecting continues automatically a little later.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 (Entra ID)
docs.text: Colleagues sign in with their Microsoft 365 account (button Sign in with Microsoft 365 on the sign-in page) and get their role from a Microsoft 365 group. Set it up under Administration → Roles & sign-in.

docs.title: 1. App registration
docs.text:
1. Open the Entra admin center → Identity → Applications → App registrations → New registration.
  2. Name: Stats Collector. Supported account types: Accounts in this organizational directory only (single tenant).
  3. Redirect URI: platform Web, value: copy it from Roles & sign-in → Redirect URI in Stats Collector (it looks like https://stats.example.org/api/auth/entra/callback).
  4. Click Register. Copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID into Stats Collector.
  5. Certificates & secrets → New client secret, valid for 24 months. Copy the Value (not the ID) into Client secret. Put a reminder in your calendar to renew it.
  6. Token configuration → Add groups claim → Security groups, for the ID token, format Group ID.
  7. API permissions: openid, profile, email and User.Read (delegated) are enough. Click Grant admin consent.

docs.title: 2. Groups for roles
docs.text:
Create four security groups in Microsoft 365 (names are an example):

Role Group Admin SC-Admins Editor-in-chief SC-EditorsInChief Editor SC-Editors Staff everyone else in the organisation (no group needed)

Copy each group's Object ID into Roles & sign-in → Roles from Microsoft 365 groups. Several IDs per role can be separated by commas, and the value of an app role (App registration → App roles) works too. Membership is read at every sign-in, so adding or removing someone in Microsoft 365 changes their role the next time they sign in. When someone is in several groups, the highest role wins (Admin, then Editor-in-chief, Editor, Staff); someone in none of the groups gets the role under Role for everyone else in the organisation.

When a person is a member of more than about 200 groups, Microsoft leaves the groups out of the sign-in token. Stats Collector then reads them from Microsoft Graph; for that add the delegated permission GroupMember.Read.All with admin consent.

docs.title: 3. Switch it on and test
docs.text:
1. Fill in the tenant ID, client ID and client secret, map the groups and switch on Enable Microsoft 365 sign-in. Click Save.
  2. Open the sign-in page in a private browser window and click Sign in with Microsoft 365.
  3. After signing in you land on the dashboard; your role is shown at the bottom of the menu. Users lists the account with sign-in method Microsoft 365.

Does it fail? The sign-in page shows the reason, for example a wrong client secret or redirect URI. The most common mistake is a redirect URI that does not match exactly: it must be the https:// address users open, so check SC_PUBLIC_URL (see Reverse proxy).

docs.title: 4. Local accounts
docs.text:
An existing local account with the same e-mail address is linked on the first Microsoft sign-in. It keeps its password and the role set in Stats Collector, so your first administrator stays a working break-glass account. Accounts created by Microsoft sign-in get their role from Microsoft 365 at every sign-in.

Keep Also allow local accounts to sign in on until Microsoft 365 sign-in works. Administrators can always sign in with a local account, so a broken Entra configuration never locks you out.

docs.title: Sources: Owncast and Icecast
docs.text: Add your streaming servers under Administration → Sources. Each server is polled every 30 seconds for the number of viewers (Owncast) or listeners (Icecast). You can add 2 to 5 of each, or more.

docs.title: Add a source
docs.text:
1. Click Add source and pick Icecast (radio) or Owncast (video).
  2. Fill in a Name (shown on the dashboard) and the Server address.
  3. Optionally fill in the admin password (see below).
  4. Click Test connection. You see the server name and, for Icecast, the mount points and their listeners right now.
  5. Click Save. The first numbers appear on the dashboard within a minute.

The status column shows Working after a successful poll, or the reason the last poll failed (wrong password, server not reachable, ...). Poll now (the round arrow) polls straight away. Switching off Collect from this source pauses it without losing its numbers. Deleting a source also deletes all its numbers.

docs.title: Icecast
docs.text:
• Server address: the address of Icecast itself, e.g. https://radio.example.org:8000, without /status-json.xsl.
  • Mount points: e.g. /live, /jazz. Leave empty to collect every mount the server reports. A configured mount that is not broadcasting counts as zero.
  • Admin user and password (optional): <admin-user> and <admin-password> from icecast.xml. With it Stats Collector also reads the average listening time and which players are used (VLC, browser, smart speaker...). IP addresses of listeners are never stored.

Stats Collector reads status-json.xsl, available in Icecast 2.4 and later.

docs.title: Owncast
docs.text:
• Server address: the address of your Owncast server, e.g. https://live.example.org.
  • Admin password (optional): the Owncast admin password. Without it the public status is used, which gives the same viewer numbers.

Every broadcast becomes a separate item with its title and start and end time, so you can compare broadcasts under Top broadcasts and streams on the dashboard.

docs.title: Webhook (recommended)
docs.text: After saving, the edit window shows a Webhook for Owncast URL. In Owncast go to Integrations → Webhooks → Create webhook, paste the URL and select Stream started and Stream stopped. Broadcasts then start and end on the minute instead of at the next poll. The URL contains a secret; if it leaks, click Renew next to it and update the webhook in Owncast.

docs.title: Network
docs.text: The Stats Collector server must be able to reach these addresses. When a source sits on the internal network, use its internal address. A self-signed certificate works if you switch off Verify the server certificate.

docs.title: Reverse proxy and HTTPS (Zoraxy)
docs.text: Stats Collector listens on plain HTTP port 8080. A reverse proxy in front of it handles HTTPS with a Let's Encrypt certificate. The live wall (from phase 3) uses port 8081 and its own host name.

docs.title: Zoraxy, step by step
docs.text:
1. DNS: create an A record (and AAAA if you use IPv6) for stats.example.org pointing to the Zoraxy server. Later add live.example.org for the live wall.
  2. Open the Zoraxy web interface and go to HTTP Proxy → Create Proxy Rules.
  3. Fill in:
  4. Proxy type: Sub-domain
  5. Matching keyword / domain: stats.example.org
  6. Target IP address or domain name with port: <ip-of-stats-server>:8080
  7. Proxy target require TLS connection: off (the app speaks HTTP behind the proxy)
  8. Create Credentials: off
  9. Click Create Endpoint.
  10. Go to TLS / SSL certificates → ACME. Enter your email address, choose Let's Encrypt, add stats.example.org and request the certificate. Enable automatic renewal.
  11. In the proxy rule, enable Force HTTPS redirect (HTTP → HTTPS).
  12. On the Stats Collector server, make sure the Zoraxy IP is in SC_TRUSTED_PROXIES in /etc/stats-collector/config.env and that SC_PUBLIC_URL starts with https://. After changing it run systemctl restart stats-collector-web.

Check it: open https://stats.example.org. Under Info & updates the page loads without warnings, and after signing in the session cookie is marked Secure.

docs.title: Why the trusted proxy IP matters
docs.text: The app only believes the X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto headers when they come from an IP in SC_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Anyone else could otherwise pretend to be another IP address, for example to dodge the login rate limit.

docs.title: Cloudflare in front of the proxy: the real visitor IP
docs.text:
When the public address goes through Cloudflare, X-Forwarded-For holds a Cloudflare address instead of the visitor's. Cloudflare sends the real address in the CF-Connecting-IP header. Tell Stats Collector to use it by adding this line to /etc/stats-collector/config.env (or run the installer with --client-ip-header CF-Connecting-IP):

SC_CLIENT_IP_HEADER=CF-Connecting-IP

and run systemctl restart stats-collector-web. The header is only read on requests from a trusted proxy, so it cannot be faked from outside. The audit log and the login rate limit then see the real visitor addresses.

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text: When Zoraxy runs on another machine, only Zoraxy needs to reach port 8080. Run the installer again with --firewall to have nftables enforce this.

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
server {
    server_name stats.example.org;
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    # ssl_certificate lines from certbot
    client_max_body_size 10m;
    location / {
        proxy_pass http://10.0.0.20:8080;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
stats.example.org {
    reverse_proxy 10.0.0.20:8080
}

docs.title: Traefik (labels)
docs.text:
- traefik.http.routers.stats.rule=Host(`stats.example.org`)
- traefik.http.routers.stats.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
- traefik.http.services.stats.loadbalancer.server.port=8080

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: What Command Web application journalctl -u stats-collector-web -f Updates, backups, restores journalctl -u stats-collector-ops -n 200, or the log on the page while it runs Logs of earlier tasks /var/lib/stats-collector/ops/job-<id>.log pgBackRest /var/log/pgbackrest/ PostgreSQL journalctl -u postgresql@17-main

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
stats-collector version             # installed version and channel
stats-collector setup-link          # one-time link for the first administrator
stats-collector reset-password EMAIL
stats-collector migrate             # apply database migrations
stats-collector ops run-pending     # run queued tasks now (root)
stats-collector backup full|incr    # make a backup now (root)
stats-collector restore --target ID --label LABEL   # restore from a remote location (root)

docs.title: Common problems
docs.text:
The page does not load through the proxy. Check curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/health on the server. If that works, check the proxy rule and that port 8080 is reachable from the proxy (firewall).

I am logged out immediately after signing in. The public URL starts with https:// but the proxy sends plain HTTP to the browser, or the other way round. Make SC_PUBLIC_URL match the address in the browser.

The dashboard shows no numbers. Check Administration → Sources: the status column shows why a source fails. When every source stays on Waiting for first poll, the worker is not running: systemctl status stats-collector-worker and journalctl -u stats-collector-worker -n 50. The worker needs Redis (systemctl status redis-server).

A task stays "Queued". The ops runner is not running: systemctl status stats-collector-ops.path. Start it with systemctl enable --now stats-collector-ops.path. Queued tasks are also picked up by the hourly run (five past the hour); to start them right away, run sudo stats-collector ops run-pending.

"GitHub cannot be reached". The server needs outgoing HTTPS to api.github.com and github.com to check for and download updates.

Backup test fails with "permission denied" on SFTP. Check the username and key, and that the folder can be created by that user. For key login paste the complete private key including the BEGIN and END lines.

The update failed. The previous version and the database were restored automatically. The task log on the Info page shows the reason. Report it with that log.

docs.title: Info, updates and the production/test channel
docs.text: Click Info & updates at the bottom of the left menu. A dot next to it means an update is available.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: The Version card shows the installed version, the channel, the git commit, the build date and, for administrators, the database, operating system and free disk space.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel Follows For Production Releases from the main branch Daily use Test Test builds from the develop branch (and production releases) A test server, or trying new features early

Switch with the Production / Test buttons. Switching only changes which releases are offered; nothing is installed until you click Update now or Install.

docs.title: Checking and installing updates
docs.text:
Check for updates asks GitHub for the newest releases (the result is cached for ten minutes otherwise). When a newer version exists for your channel, Update now appears.

An update:

  1. downloads the release and checks its SHA-256 checksum;
  2. makes a database dump;
  3. installs the new version next to the current one, with its own Python environment;
  4. runs the database migrations;
  5. switches over and restarts the web service;
  6. checks that the new version responds. If it does not, the previous version and the database dump are restored automatically.

The page shows the log while this runs and reloads when it is finished. The last three versions stay on disk.

docs.title: Releases and release notes
docs.text:
The Releases list shows every version with its channel and date. The tabs New, Changed, Removed and Fixed show what changed, in your language. Install puts any listed version on the server, for example to go back from a test build to the newest production release. When the target version is older, the database schema is migrated down first.

The same notes are in CHANGELOG.md and on the GitHub releases page.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text: Sign in with your email address and password. After ten wrong attempts from the same address within five minutes, the login is blocked for a few minutes.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
Every local account can turn on two-factor authentication: My profile (click your initials at the bottom of the menu) → Two-factor authentication → Turn on. Add the key to an authenticator app such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or 1Password and enter the code it shows. From then on, sign-in asks for the 6-digit code.

Lost your phone? An administrator on the server can reset the password, which also switches two-factor authentication off:

stats-collector reset-password name@example.org

docs.title: Users
docs.text: Administrators manage accounts in Administration → Users: add, change role, disable, reset a password or delete. There is always at least one active administrator; the app refuses to remove the last one.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Role Sees Can Admin Everything Sources, users, branding, email, backup, updates, live walls Editor-in-chief Everything, including numbers per editor Dashboards, reports and goals; send reports Editor All items and channels, plus their own editor numbers Own dashboards, on-demand reports Staff All items, channels, followers and goals without editor names View only

Editor names and per-editor numbers are removed on the server before data reaches the browser of Staff and Editors.

docs.title: Microsoft 365
docs.text: From phase 1 colleagues can sign in with their Microsoft 365 account and get their role from a Microsoft 365 group. The settings can already be prepared: see Microsoft 365.

docs.title: WordPress
docs.text:
Stats Collector has its own WordPress plugin. It counts per article, without cookies, how often it is viewed, by how many visitors, how long people read, whether they read it, where they came from (Google, Facebook…), which device they use and how often the share buttons are clicked. Every minute it sends these numbers to Stats Collector, together with the title, author, category and tags of each article, so you can see numbers per editor.

No cookie banner is needed: the plugin does not set cookies and does not store IP addresses. A visitor is recognised for one day only, by a code made from the IP address, the browser and a random value that changes every night. The next day the same person counts as a new visitor, and the code can never be turned back into an IP address.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• WordPress 6.5 or newer, PHP 8.1 or newer.
  • The WordPress server can reach your Stats Collector over HTTPS (outgoing).
  • Stats Collector is reachable at its public address (see Reverse proxy).

docs.title: Step 1: add the site in Stats Collector
docs.text:
1. Go to Administration → Sources → Add source and choose WordPress (website).
  2. Fill in a name (for example the name of the website) and the address of the website. Click Save.
  3. The dialog now shows three values: the Stats Collector address for the plugin, the site key and the secret. Copy the secret now: it is shown only once.
  4. Click Download WordPress plugin to get stats-collector-wordpress.zip.

Lost the secret? Open the site under Sources and click New key and secret. The plugin stops sending until you paste the new values in WordPress.

docs.title: Step 2: install the plugin in WordPress
docs.text:
1. In WordPress go to Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin, choose stats-collector-wordpress.zip and click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Go to Settings → Stats Collector.
  3. Fill in Stats Collector address (only the address, for example https://stats.example.org), the site key and the secret. Click Save settings.
  4. Click Test connection. You should see Connection works.

Repeat this for every website. Each website is a separate source with its own key.

docs.title: Plugin settings
docs.text:
Setting What it does Content types Which kinds of content are counted per item (posts and pages by default). The home page always counts towards the site total. Own visits When on (default), logged-in editors and administrators are not counted. Behind a proxy or CDN Choose CF-Connecting-IP when the website is behind Cloudflare, X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP behind another proxy. Otherwise every visitor looks the same and unique visitors are undercounted. Editors Sends the email address of authors so Stats Collector can link them to their account (see below).

The Status block shows when the last batch was sent and the last error. Send now sends straight away.

docs.title: What is counted
docs.text:
Number Meaning Views Every time an article is opened. A reload by the same visitor within 30 minutes counts once. Search engines and other bots are left out. Visitors Different visitors. Per day these are real unique visitors; over a longer period the days are added up (the same person on two days counts twice, because the plugin forgets visitors every night). Reading time The time the article was visible on screen while the reader was active (scrolling, moving the mouse, touching), at most 30 minutes per view. Avg. reading time is the reading time divided by the views. Read A view in which someone read for at least 30 seconds, or scrolled through three quarters of the page in at least 10 seconds. Shares Clicks on share links for Facebook, X, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Telegram, Bluesky, Reddit, Pinterest and email. Your own share button counts too when it has the attribute data-sc-share. Comments Approved comments per hour. Referrers and devices Per day the site that sent the visitor (direct when unknown) and the type of device: mobile, desktop or tablet.

Returning visitors are not counted, because that is not possible without cookies.

The plugin keeps the raw page views for 35 days in its own table (wp_sc_views) so it can resend after an outage. The numbers themselves are stored in Stats Collector for good.

docs.title: Editors
docs.text:
Each WordPress author becomes an editor in Stats Collector. When the email address of the WordPress user is the same as the email address of a Stats Collector user (local or Microsoft 365), they are linked: that user then sees their own numbers under Editors. Co-authors are supported when the Co-Authors Plus plugin is installed.

See Content and editors for what each role can see.

docs.title: Sending every minute
docs.text:
WordPress runs its scheduled tasks when someone visits the site. On a busy website that is every minute anyway. On a quiet site, let the server call WordPress every minute and turn off the built-in trigger:

  1. Add to wp-config.php: define('DISABLE_WP_CRON', true);
  2. Add a cron job on the web server: * * * * * curl -fsS https://www.example.org/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron >/dev/null

If the connection is down for a while, the plugin catches up by itself, 24 hours per minute, for up to 35 days.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text: Message Solution the site key or secret is wrong Copy both again from Stats Collector, or make a new key and secret. the clock of this server is more than five minutes off Turn on time synchronisation (NTP) on the web server. this site is paused in Stats Collector Turn Collect from this source back on under Sources. A connection error (cURL) The web server cannot reach Stats Collector: check the address, the firewall and the HTTPS certificate. No numbers although the test works Check that WordPress cron runs (Next batch in the status should be within a minute) and that you are not testing while logged in as an editor.

docs.title: YouTube
docs.text: Stats Collector reads your YouTube channel with the YouTube Data API v3 (videos, subscriber count) and the YouTube Analytics API (views, watch time, likes, comments, shares, subscribers gained and lost). After connecting, it imports the whole history of the channel, back to the day it was created, and then keeps it up to date every three hours.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
Number Per Note Views, watch time, average view duration Channel and video, per day Average view duration = watch time ÷ views Likes, comments, shares Channel and video, per day Subscribers gained and lost Channel, per day Subscribers Channel, per day See below
  • YouTube Analytics has numbers per day, not per hour, and they arrive one to two days late. Today and yesterday therefore fill in later; Stats Collector reads the last five days again at every run.
  • Per video, the 200 most viewed videos of each day are stored. For a regional channel that is every video that was watched that day.
  • Subscribers per day: YouTube only gives today's count. Stats Collector works the earlier days back from it with the daily gains and losses, so the history is a close estimate (YouTube corrects spam subscribers now and then, which the daily numbers do not show).
  • Videos that were deleted or made private keep their numbers; they show their video ID instead of the title.

The numbers appear on the Dashboard (card Website and video) and on the Content page, where every video is an item. See Content and editors.

docs.title: 1. Google Cloud project
docs.text:
1. Open console.cloud.google.com with the Google account that owns or manages the YouTube channel → New project, for example Stats Collector.
  2. APIs & Services → Library: enable YouTube Data API v3 and YouTube Analytics API.

docs.title: 2. OAuth consent screen
docs.text:
1. APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen (in newer consoles: Google Auth Platform → Branding / Audience). User type External, unless the channel belongs to your own Google Workspace; then Internal needs no verification.
  2. App name Stats Collector, support email, home page (https://stats.example.org), privacy policy URL and authorised domain (example.org).
  3. Scopes (Data access): https://www.googleapis.com/auth/youtube.readonly and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/yt-analytics.readonly.
  4. While the app is in Testing, add the Google account that manages the channel as a test user. In testing mode Google ends the access after 7 days; Stats Collector then shows Access to YouTube has ended and you connect again. Publish the app (Audience → Publish app) and complete Google's verification to avoid that.

docs.title: 3. OAuth client
docs.text:
1. In Stats Collector go to Administration → Sources → Add source, choose YouTube (channel) and copy the Redirect address for Google shown in the dialog. It is https://<your Stats Collector address>/api/connectors/youtube/callback.
  2. In Google Cloud: APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID, type Web application. Under Authorised redirect URIs paste the redirect address. Click Create and copy the client ID and client secret.

docs.title: 4. Connect the channel
docs.text:
1. Back in Stats Collector paste the client ID and client secret, give the source a name and click Save.
  2. Click Connect with Google. Sign in with the account that manages the channel. For a channel on a brand account, choose that brand account when Google asks which channel or account to use. Allow both permissions.
  3. You return to Sources with YouTube channel connected. The dialog shows the channel, its subscribers and videos, and how far the history import has come.

The history is imported in steps of about 120 days per quarter of an hour, so a channel that is ten years old is complete in about eight hours. The channel totals per day are there right away.

docs.title: Disconnecting
docs.text: Disconnect in the dialog withdraws the access at Google and stops collecting. The numbers collected so far stay. To connect another channel with the same Google app, add a new YouTube source with the same client ID and secret.

docs.title: Problems
docs.text: Message Solution Google did not accept the code The client secret is wrong, or the redirect address in Google Cloud is not exactly the one shown in Stats Collector (check https, the host name and that there is no trailing slash). Not all permissions were granted Connect again and tick both boxes on the Google screen. This Google account has no YouTube channel Sign in with the account (or brand account) of the channel. Access to YouTube has ended Connect again. In testing mode this happens every 7 days; publish the app to stop it. YouTube refused access Enable both APIs in the Google Cloud project. The daily YouTube quota is used up Collecting continues the next day. The Data API allows 10,000 units a day; Stats Collector normally uses a few hundred. The sign-in with Google took too long Start again with Connect with Google and finish within 10 minutes.

docs.title: Handleiding Stats Collector
docs.text:
Stats Collector verzamelt bereik, interactie en publieksaantallen van je website, social media en streams, en brengt die samen in één dashboard en in rapporten. Deze handleiding legt uit hoe je het installeert, hoe je alles instelt en hoe je elk platform koppelt.

Dezelfde handleiding opent in de applicatie via de knop Help onderaan het linkermenu. Die versie hoort altijd bij de geïnstalleerde versie.

Deze handleiding groeit mee met elke release. Pagina's over koppelingen die nog niet gebouwd zijn beschrijven de voorbereiding die je nu al kunt doen, zodat de accounts klaarstaan als de koppeling komt.

docs.title: Aan de slag
docs.text:
1. Installatie op Debian 13
  2. Reverse proxy en HTTPS (Zoraxy)
  3. Eerste keer inloggen, gebruikers en rollen
  4. Huisstijl
  5. E-mail (SMTP)
  6. Back-up en herstel
  7. Info, updates en het productie-/testkanaal

docs.title: Gebruiken
docs.text:
• Dashboard
  • Content en redacteuren
  • Mijn dashboards
  • Volgers en doelen

docs.title: Platforms koppelen
docs.text: Platform Pagina Beschikbaar vanaf Inloggen met Microsoft 365 (Entra ID) Microsoft 365 Fase 1 (instellingen kun je nu al voorbereiden) Owncast en Icecast Owncast en Icecast Fase 1 WordPress (eigen plugin) WordPress Beschikbaar YouTube YouTube Beschikbaar Facebook en Instagram Meta: Facebook en Instagram Beschikbaar

docs.title: Als er iets misgaat
docs.text: Problemen oplossen noemt de logbestanden, de opdrachten voor de command line en de meest voorkomende problemen.

docs.title: Back-up en herstel
docs.text: Beheer → Back-up & herstel maakt volledige en incrementele back-ups van de database en de bestanden (geüploade logo's en het configuratiebestand) en kopieert ze naar een of meer externe locaties.

docs.title: Hoe het werkt
docs.text:
• De database wordt geback-upt met pgBackRest. Een volledige back-up bevat alles; een incrementele alleen wat er sinds de vorige back-up veranderd is. PostgreSQL archiveert zijn transactielog doorlopend, dus back-ups zijn consistent terwijl de app gewoon doordraait.
  • Bestanden worden met tar in incrementele modus ingepakt.
  • Na elke back-up wordt de hele lokale back-upmap (/var/lib/stats-collector/backup) met rclone gesynchroniseerd naar elke ingeschakelde externe locatie.
  • Met een versleutelingswachtwoord worden de kopieën op de externe locatie versleuteld (rclone crypt: XSalsa20-Poly1305). Zonder dat wachtwoord kan niemand ze lezen, jij ook niet, dus bewaar het in je wachtwoordmanager.

docs.title: Externe locaties
docs.text:
Klik op Locatie toevoegen en kies een protocol:

Protocol Wanneer Opmerkingen SCP / SFTP (SSH) NAS, Linux-server, hosting met SSH Wachtwoord of privésleutel (OpenSSH- of PEM-formaat). Bij de eerste Test wordt de hostsleutel van de server opgeslagen en daarna steeds gecontroleerd. FTPS NAS of hosting met FTP over TLS Expliciet (poort 21, AUTH TLS) komt het meest voor; impliciet gebruikt poort 990. FTP Alleen op een vertrouwd netwerk Het wachtwoord gaat onversleuteld over het netwerk.

Map is het pad op de externe server; die wordt automatisch aangemaakt. Klik op Testen om de verbinding te controleren: het logboek toont elke stap en de back-ups die er al staan.

docs.title: Planning en bewaartermijn
docs.text:
• Automatisch back-ups maken: aan of uit.
  • Volledige back-up elke dag, week (kies de dag) of maand, op het gekozen tijdstip (tijdzone uit Algemene instellingen).
  • Incrementele back-up elke N uur daartussen.
  • Volledige back-ups bewaren: hoeveel volledige back-ups (met hun incrementele) bewaard blijven. Oudere worden lokaal en op de externe locaties verwijderd.

Nu volledige back-up en Nu incrementele back-up starten er direct een. Het logboek verschijnt op de pagina.

docs.title: Herstellen
docs.text:
1. Kies onder Herstellen een locatie en klik op Back-ups tonen. De lijst komt van de externe locatie zelf, dus dit werkt ook op een gloednieuwe server.
  2. Klik op Herstellen naast het moment waar je naar terug wilt. Kies je een incrementele back-up, dan wordt de volledige back-up plus alle incrementele tot dat moment teruggezet.
  3. Typ RESTORE en bevestig. De applicatie stopt, database en bestanden worden vervangen en de applicatie start weer. Log daarna opnieuw in.

docs.title: Noodherstel op een nieuwe server
docs.text:
1. Installeer Stats Collector met het installatiescript op de nieuwe server.
  2. Maak via de installatielink een tijdelijke beheerder aan.
  3. Stel onder Back-up & herstel hetzelfde versleutelingswachtwoord in en voeg de externe locatie toe.
  4. Toon de back-ups en zet de nieuwste terug. De teruggezette configuratie bevat de oorspronkelijke geheime sleutel, dus opgeslagen wachtwoorden blijven werken.

docs.title: Voor elke update
docs.text: Updates vanuit de interface maken eerst een extra databasedump in /var/lib/stats-collector/backup/pre-update/ en gebruiken die om automatisch terug te draaien als de update mislukt.

docs.title: Huisstijl
docs.text:
Beheer → Huisstijl bepaalt het uiterlijk van de applicatie, rapporten, e-mails en de live wall.

  • Naam en logo: naam van de applicatie, een logo voor lichte achtergronden, een logo voor donkere achtergronden (gebruikt in het donkere menu) en het browsericoon. SVG, PNG, WebP of ICO tot 2 MB. SVG-bestanden met scripts worden geweigerd.
  • Kleuren: accent, achtergrond, kaarten, menu, tekst, lijnen en de statuskleuren, apart voor licht en donker thema. Het voorbeeld verandert mee. Tekst op de accentkleur wisselt automatisch tussen zwart en wit voor de leesbaarheid.
  • Kleuren per kanaal: de kleur van elk platform in grafieken (website, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Owncast, Icecast).
  • Typografie en vorm: lettertype voor koppen en tekst, hoekafronding van kaarten en knoppen.

Klik op Opslaan om de huisstijl voor iedereen toe te passen. Terug naar standaard zet de ingebouwde huisstijl uit branding/default/theme.json terug.

docs.title: Exporteren, importeren en de repository
docs.text: Huisstijl exporteren downloadt een theme.json. Zet die in de repository van het project als branding/<naam>/theme.json, samen met de logobestanden, zodat elke huisstijl in versiebeheer staat. Huisstijl importeren laadt zo'n bestand; klik daarna op Opslaan.

docs.title: Licht en donker thema
docs.text: Elke gebruiker kiest Systeem, Licht of Donker onder Mijn profiel → Weergave. Systeem volgt de instelling van de computer.

docs.title: Content
docs.text:
Analyse → Content toont de artikelen, uitzendingen en streams met de meeste weergaven of luister- en kijkminuten in de gekozen periode (24 uur, 7, 30 of 90 dagen, of 12 maanden). Iedereen kan deze pagina openen.

  • Zoek in titels, Bron, Categorie en Redacteur maken de lijst kleiner. Het filter op redacteur is er alleen voor rollen die redacteuren mogen zien (zie hieronder).
  • Sorteer zet de lijst op volgorde van weergaven, bezoekers, leestijd, gelezen, gedeeld, reacties of luister-/kijkminuten, of toont de nieuwste items eerst.

  • Kolommen: Weergaven, Bezoekers, Gem. leestijd (leestijd gedeeld door weergaven), Gelezen, Gedeeld en Luister-/kijkmin. voor uitzendingen en mountpoints. Zie WordPress voor de betekenis van elk cijfer.

  • Facebook- en Instagram-berichten en YouTube-video's staan in dezelfde lijst. Bij een bericht toont Bezoekers / bereik het bereik. Zie Meta en YouTube voor hoe die cijfers verzameld worden.

Klik op een item voor de details: de cijfers over de periode, een grafiek per dag (per uur bij 24 uur), en bij een artikel waar lezers vandaan kwamen en welke apparaten ze gebruikten. Een Facebook-bericht toont ook de reacties per soort (leuk, geweldig, wauw…); een Instagram-bericht hoe vaak het is opgeslagen.

docs.title: Redacteuren
docs.text:
Analyse → Redacteuren toont de cijfers per redacteur: hoeveel van hun artikelen in de periode zijn gepubliceerd, en de weergaven, bezoekers, leestijd, gelezen artikelen, keren gedeeld en reacties van al hun artikelen in die periode. Een artikel met twee auteurs telt voor allebei.

De kolom Sociale weergaven telt de weergaven op van de Facebook- en Instagram-berichten en YouTube-video's die naar de artikelen van de redacteur linken (zie Berichten gekoppeld aan artikelen). Klik op een redacteur voor een grafiek, de best gelezen artikelen en de sociale cijfers per platform, met de gekoppelde berichten.

docs.title: Berichten gekoppeld aan artikelen
docs.text:
Een Facebook-bericht, Instagram-bericht of YouTube-video wordt automatisch aan een artikel gekoppeld als het naar het adres van dat artikel verwijst:

  • Facebook: de link die bij het bericht is gevoegd, of een link in de tekst.
  • Instagram: een link in het bijschrift (op Instagram staan links meestal in de bio, koppel die berichten dan met de hand).
  • YouTube: een link in de videobeschrijving.

Adressen worden vergeleken zonder https://, www. of een / aan het eind, en zonder trackingparameters zoals utm_source of fbclid; de doorstuurlinks van Facebook worden gevolgd naar het echte adres. De korte link ?p=123 van een WordPress-bericht werkt ook. De koppelingen worden elke 15 minuten bijgewerkt, nadat nieuwe berichten zijn opgehaald.

Open een artikel om onder Gedeeld op sociale media de berichten en video's te zien die ernaar linken, met hun weergaven, bereik, likes en keren gedeeld, en het totaal als Sociale weergaven. Een bericht toont zijn Gekoppeld artikel. Klik op een titel om dat item te openen.

Beheerders, hoofdredacteuren en redacteuren kunnen koppelingen aanpassen:

  • Koppeling toevoegen zoekt artikelen (vanuit een bericht) of berichten en video's (vanuit een artikel) op titel of adres; klik op een resultaat om het te koppelen. De koppeling heet dan handmatig.
  • De ontkoppelknop haalt een koppeling weg. Een weggehaalde automatische koppeling blijft weg, ook als het bericht opnieuw wordt opgehaald; met de hand toevoegen brengt hem terug.

De sociale cijfers van een redacteur tellen elk bericht dat aan een van zijn of haar artikelen is gekoppeld. Een bericht bij een artikel met twee auteurs telt voor allebei.

docs.title: Wie ziet wat
docs.text:
Namen van redacteuren en cijfers per redacteur worden door de server weggehaald voordat er iets naar de browser gaat, dus ze zijn ook niet in de pagina terug te vinden.

Rol Content Redacteuren Beheerder, Hoofdredacteur Alle items, met namen van redacteuren en het filter op redacteur Iedereen Redacteur Alle items, zonder namen van redacteuren Alleen de eigen cijfers Medewerker Alle items, zonder namen van redacteuren Niet beschikbaar

Een redacteur ziet de eigen cijfers als het Stats Collector-account hetzelfde e-mailadres heeft als de WordPress-gebruiker. Niet gekoppeld aan een gebruiker onder Redacteuren betekent dat er nog geen account met dat e-mailadres is.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Het dashboard is het eerste scherm na het inloggen. Iedereen kan het openen, welke rol je ook hebt.

docs.title: Website en video
docs.text: Is er een WordPress-site, YouTube-kanaal, Facebook-pagina of Instagram-account gekoppeld, dan begint het dashboard met de kaart Website en video: de weergaven van alle kanalen samen met hun totale bereik, een tegel per website (paginaweergaven en bezoekers), per YouTube-kanaal (weergaven, bekeken minuten, abonnees en hoeveel erbij kwamen in de periode) en per Facebook-pagina of Instagram-account (weergaven, bereik, volgers en hoeveel erbij kwamen), en een grafiek met de weergaven per uur (24 uur) of per dag, gestapeld per kanaal. YouTube-cijfers komen een tot twee dagen later binnen, dus de laatste dagen van de grafiek vullen zich later aan. YouTube, Facebook en Instagram geven alleen hele dagen: in de weergave 24 uur staat in hun tegel alleen cijfers per dag en ontbreken ze in de grafiek. Topcontent opent de pagina Content.

docs.title: Nu live
docs.text:
• Nu live: iedereen die op dit moment luistert en kijkt, over alle bronnen samen. De rode stip knippert zolang minstens één bron in de lucht is.
  • Piek vandaag: het hoogste publiek van elke bron vandaag, opgeteld.
  • Luister- en kijkminuten en Hoogste piek: totalen over de periode die je rechtsboven kiest (24 uur, 7, 30 of 90 dagen).

Daaronder staat per bron een tegel met het publiek op dit moment en de piek van vandaag. Bij een Icecast-server met meerdere mountpoints staat elke mount apart; bij Owncast zie je de titel van de lopende uitzending. Een rode regel in een tegel betekent dat de laatste ophaalronde mislukte; de reden staat erbij, en onder Beheer → Bronnen vind je de details.

De tegels verversen elke 15 seconden.

docs.title: Grafiek live publiek
docs.text:
• Gemiddeld, Piek, Minuten: wat de grafiek laat zien. Gemiddeld is het aantal mensen dat tegelijk luistert of kijkt, Minuten de totale luister- en kijktijd.
  • Gestapeld telt de bronnen op tot één totaal, Over elkaar tekent ze over elkaar heen, Apart geeft elke bron een eigen kleine grafiek.
  • Klik op een naam in de legenda onder de grafiek om die bron te verbergen of weer te tonen.

Bij 24 uur is elk punt 5 minuten, bij 7 dagen een uur, bij 30 en 90 dagen een dag. Dagen volgen de tijdzone onder Algemene instellingen.

docs.title: Per bron en best bekeken uitzendingen
docs.text: Per bron geeft minuten, gemiddelde en piek per bron in de periode. Best bekeken uitzendingen en streams toont de Owncast-uitzendingen en Icecast-mounts met de meeste minuten.

docs.title: Hoe de cijfers worden geteld
docs.text:
Elke bron wordt elke 30 seconden opgehaald (per bron in te stellen). Bij elke ophaalronde wordt het aantal luisteraars of kijkers op dat moment opgeslagen. Elke 5 minuten worden die metingen opgeteld tot totalen per uur, dag en maand:

  • minuten = luisteraars × tijd tussen twee ophaalrondes;
  • gemiddeld = minuten gedeeld door de lengte van het uur of de dag (tijd uit de lucht telt als nul);
  • piek = het hoogste aantal in één ophaalronde.

Lag de verzamelaar zelf stil, dan wordt dat gat niet opgevuld. Ruwe metingen worden een jaar bewaard; totalen per uur en per dag blijven altijd bewaard.

docs.title: Mijn dashboards
docs.text: Analyse → Mijn dashboards laat je je eigen overzichten van de cijfers maken: totalen, grafieken per platform of per bron, topcontent, de ranglijst van redacteuren en doelen, naast elkaar. Iedereen kan dashboards voor zichzelf maken; beheerders en hoofdredacteuren kunnen een dashboard ook met iedereen delen.

docs.title: Een dashboard gebruiken
docs.text:
• De tabbladen bovenaan zijn jouw dashboards en de gedeelde (met het deel-icoon). De app onthoudt welke je het laatst open had.
  • De periode rechtsboven (24 uur, 7, 30 of 90 dagen, 12 maanden) geldt voor alle widgets.
  • Een totaal toont het cijfer over de periode en hoeveel het steeg of daalde ten opzichte van de periode ervoor (bij 30 dagen: de 30 dagen daarvoor).
  • Een grafiek kan wisselen tussen Gestapeld (de lijnen tellen op tot één totaal), Over elkaar (lijnen over elkaar heen) en Los (een kleine grafiek per platform of bron). Iedereen kan wisselen; alleen wie het dashboard mag bewerken slaat het op als standaard.
  • Klik op een naam in de legenda onder een grafiek om die te verbergen of te tonen.
  • Klik in Topcontent op een titel voor de details.

docs.title: Maatstaven
docs.text:
De cijfers van elk platform worden opgeteld in vijf gedeelde maatstaven, zodat kanalen tot één totaal gestapeld kunnen worden:

Maatstaf Telt Bereik Websitebezoekers plus het bereik op Facebook en Instagram Weergaven Paginaweergaven, weergaven op YouTube en weergaven van Facebook- en Instagram-berichten Interacties Likes, reacties, opmerkingen, keren gedeeld en opgeslagen (website: gedeeld en reacties) Kijk- en luisterminuten Kijkminuten op YouTube plus minuten via Owncast en Icecast Volgers Abonnees op YouTube plus volgers op Facebook en Instagram, per dag

Bereik wordt per dag geteld, dus iemand die op twee dagen terugkomt telt twee keer. YouTube, Facebook en Instagram geven alleen hele dagen door: bij 24 uur staan ze niet in een grafiek (de widget meldt dat), en Volgers toont altijd dagen.

docs.title: Een dashboard bouwen
docs.text:
Klik op Nieuw dashboard, of op Bewerken bij een dashboard dat je mag aanpassen. Heb je nog geen dashboards, dan geeft Voorbeelddashboard maken een kant-en-klaar begin (bereik, weergaven en interacties, bereik per platform, volgers, interacties, topcontent en redacteuren) dat je kunt aanpassen.

Tijdens het bewerken:

  • Typ bovenaan de naam van het dashboard. Gedeeld met iedereen (beheerders en hoofdredacteuren) maakt het zichtbaar voor alle gebruikers; alleen beheerders, hoofdredacteuren en de maker kunnen het aanpassen.
  • Widget toevoegen opent het widgetformulier. Elke widget heeft pijlen om hem omhoog of omlaag te zetten, een potlood om hem aan te passen en een prullenbak om hem weg te halen.
  • Opslaan bewaart het dashboard, Annuleren gooit de wijzigingen weg, Verwijderen haalt het hele dashboard weg.

Het widgetformulier:

  • Widget: Totaal (KPI), Grafiek, Topcontent, Ranglijst redacteuren of Doelen.
  • Breedte: een derde, half of de volle breedte. Op een telefoon neemt elke widget de volle breedte.
  • Titel: laat leeg voor de naam van de maatstaf.
  • Maatstaf, Platforms en Bronnen (totaal en grafiek): wat er geteld wordt, en waarvandaan. Niets gekozen betekent alles.
  • Lijnen per (grafiek): één lijn per platform, per bron, of één totaal. Weergave en Grafiek (vlak, lijn of staven) bepalen hoe hij getekend wordt.
  • Sorteer op, Items en Aantal regels (topcontent): bijvoorbeeld de 10 best gelezen artikelen of de sociale berichten met het meeste bereik.

De Ranglijst redacteuren toont cijfers per redacteur alleen aan rollen die ze mogen zien (zie Content en redacteuren).

docs.title: E-mail (SMTP)
docs.text: Stats Collector verstuurt meldingen en (vanaf fase 4) rapporten via je eigen SMTP-server. Open Beheer → E-mail.

docs.title: Instellingen
docs.text:
Veld Uitleg E-mail versturen Hoofdschakelaar SMTP-server, poort bijv. smtp.office365.com en 587 Versleuteling STARTTLS (poort 587, aanbevolen), SSL/TLS (SMTPS, poort 465) of geen (alleen op een vertrouwd lokaal netwerk). TLS 1.2 is het minimum. Certificaat van de server controleren Laat aan. Zet alleen uit voor een interne server met een zelfondertekend certificaat. Authenticatie Gebruikersnaam en wachtwoord, OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2) of geen Afzenderadres, naam, antwoordadres Wat ontvangers zien

De knoppen Microsoft 365, Google Workspace en SMTPS (465) vullen server, poort en versleuteling in.

Wachtwoorden en geheimen worden versleuteld opgeslagen. Het scherm laat alleen zien dat er een waarde is opgeslagen; laat het veld leeg om die te behouden.

docs.title: Testen
docs.text: Vul onder Testen een adres in en klik op Testmail versturen. De instellingen worden eerst opgeslagen. Als versturen mislukt, zie je de exacte foutmelding van de mailserver, bijvoorbeeld 535 Authentication unsuccessful.

docs.title: Microsoft 365 met OAuth 2.0
docs.text:
Microsoft zet basisauthenticatie voor SMTP uit. Gebruik daarom OAuth 2.0:

  1. Ga in het Entra-beheercentrum naar App-registraties → Nieuwe registratie en noem hem Stats Collector mail.
  2. API-machtigingen → Een machtiging toevoegen → API's die mijn organisatie gebruikt → Office 365 Exchange Online → Toepassingsmachtigingen → SMTP.SendAsApp. Klik op Beheerderstoestemming verlenen.
  3. Certificaten en geheimen → Nieuw clientgeheim. Kopieer de waarde.
  4. Registreer de app in Exchange Online PowerShell en geef hem rechten op de verzendende mailbox: 
    New-ServicePrincipal -AppId <client-id> -ObjectId <object-id-enterprise-app>
Add-MailboxPermission -Identity stats@example.org -User <object-id-enterprise-app> -AccessRights FullAccess
  5. Kies in Stats Collector OAuth 2.0 (XOAUTH2):
  6. Gebruikersnaam: de mailbox, bijv. stats@example.org
  7. Token-URL: https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/v2.0/token
  8. Scope: https://outlook.office365.com/.default
  9. Client-ID en clientgeheim uit stap 1 en 3
  10. Verstuur een testmail.

Versturen via de Microsoft Graph API (in plaats van SMTP) komt samen met de rapporten in fase 4.

docs.title: Volgers
docs.text:
Analyse → Volgers toont hoe het aantal YouTube-abonnees en Facebook- en Instagram-volgers groeit, per kanaal en voor alle kanalen samen. Iedereen kan deze pagina openen.

  • Kies rechtsboven 30 dagen, 90 dagen of 12 maanden.
  • De tegels tonen het aantal nu, hoeveel het veranderde in de periode en hoeveel nieuwe volgers er kwamen (wie vertrok wordt in dat laatste getal niet afgetrokken).
  • Gestapeld zet de kanalen op elkaar, zodat de bovenste lijn het totaal is; Los toont elk kanaal op een eigen schaal.

Het aantal per dag is het aantal aan het eind van die dag. YouTube en Facebook geven de dagelijkse aanwas en het verlies over hun hele historie, dus hun lijnen gaan terug tot zover de historie is opgehaald. Instagram geeft nieuwe volgers alleen voor de laatste 30 dagen; die lijn is exact vanaf de dag dat je koppelde. Zie YouTube en Meta.

docs.title: Doelen
docs.text:
Analyse → Doelen toont de doelen met hun voortgang. Iedereen kan ze zien; de hoofdredacteur en beheerders kunnen ze toevoegen en wijzigen.

Een doel meet een van deze, over alle kanalen of de kanalen die je kiest:

Meten Het doel is gehaald als Volgers het aantal volgers en abonnees het doel haalt Weergaven pagina-, video- en berichtweergaven vanaf de startdatum samen het doel halen Bereik websitebezoekers en sociaal bereik per dag vanaf de startdatum samen het doel halen Interacties likes, reacties, opmerkingen, keren gedeeld en opgeslagen vanaf de startdatum samen het doel halen Luister- en kijkminuten live minuten en YouTube-kijktijd vanaf de startdatum samen het doel halen

Elke doelkaart toont de waarde nu, het doel, een voortgangsbalk en een status:

  • Op koers: in het tempo van de laatste twee weken wordt het doel op de einddatum gehaald;
  • Loopt achter: in dat tempo niet;
  • Gehaald en Niet gehaald (de einddatum is voorbij).

Klik op een doel voor de details: het huidige tempo en het tempo dat per dag nodig is, de prognose voor de einddatum, en een grafiek met de waarde, het doel als streepjeslijn en de trend als stippellijn.

docs.title: Een doel toevoegen en wijzigen
docs.text:
1. Nieuw doel: een naam, wat je meet, het doel, een startdatum en (optioneel) een einddatum. Kies kanalen, of geen voor alle kanalen.
  2. Zet Mail als het doel gehaald is of achterloopt aan voor een bericht. Zonder adressen gaat het naar wie het doel maakte. De mails gaan via de mailserver bij Beheer → E-mail; een doel dat achterloopt wordt hooguit één keer per week gemeld.
  3. Je kunt het doel of de einddatum altijd wijzigen. Elke wijziging blijft bewaard in de historie van het doel, met de datum, wie het deed en de reden. De grafiek toont het doel dat op elk moment gold, zodat rapportages eerlijk laten zien wat het doel toen was.
